We evaluate Wasserstein Reward Trajectory Smoothing applied to Sequential Decision Making under Human Preference to resolve Noisy human preference annotations causing oscillatory reward signal updates. Evaluated on the InnoEval benchmark (ICML 2026).
tldr: Proposes Wasserstein Reward Trajectory Smoothing to address Noisy human preference annotations causing oscillatory reward signal updates in Sequential Decision Making under Human Preference.
substrate: Sequential Decision Making under Human Preference
limitation: Noisy human preference annotations causing oscillatory reward signal updates
hypothesis: To overcome noisy human preference annotations causing oscillatory reward signal updates in Sequential Decision Making under Human Preference, we introduce a knowledge-grounded synthesis combining Wasserstein Reward Trajectory Smoothing with C_obs = 0 null-model pruning and citation maturity validation (citations >= 10).

title: InnoEval Research Investigation: Conservative Offline Q-Score Filtering for Multi-Turn Safety-Grounded Dialogues

title: InnoEval Research Investigation: Process-Supervised Rationalization Trees for Formal Logic Deduction Benchmarks
abstract: This paper investigates Formal Logic Deduction Benchmarks. We evaluate Process-Supervised Rationalization Trees applied to Formal Logic Deduction Benchmarks to resolve Process-reward models over-rewarding convoluted reasoning traces with correct final answers. title: InnoEval Research Investigation: Multi-Objective Pareto Margin Boundary for Helpful vs Harmless LLM Tradeoff
abstract: This paper investigates Helpful vs Harmless LLM Tradeoff. We evaluate Multi-Objective Pareto Margin Boundary applied to Helpful vs Harmless LLM Tradeoff to resolve Scalar weight tuning unfairly suppressing informative responses in benign safety queries. Evaluated on the InnoEval benchmark (ICML 2026).
